source.title: Wide flat minima and optimal generalization in classifying high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures
source.authors: Carlo Baldassi; E. M. Malatesta; Matteo Negri; R. Zecchina

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether flatness/local entropy relates to generalization using a Gaussian-mixture perceptron and analytical/numerical local-entropy measures; it does not test a listed version's specific setting or measure.
record.gate_note: Results include local-entropy comparisons and generalization errors for regularized MSE minimizers and replicated classifiers. Values shown only in plots are not reconstructed. The reported comparisons with cited prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a related flatness hypothesis, but none of V1–V8. Its local entropy measures volumes of nearby classifiers on synthetic Gaussian mixtures and relates them to test error. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, rank generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, or compare the specified measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, Bayes-optimal configurations occupy high-local-entropy regions of the error-counting landscape, and targeting wide regions of the differentiable MSE landscape is a viable strategy in this Gaussian-mixture model. Extension to deeper architectures remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical and numerical study of a convex threshold-linear classifier on high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures; uses local entropy and replica-based algorithms rather than the listed versions' architectures and tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: In the balanced case, local entropy and generalization vary with regularization strength and replica angle; in the unbalanced case, results vary with bias, norm, and number of replicas.

fits_no_version.finding: Better-generalizing regularized MSE configurations have higher normalized local entropy in balanced and unbalanced Gaussian mixtures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a linear classifier on Gaussian mixtures, scale-normalized local entropy of the error-counting landscape tracks generalization error across the studied regularization and bias choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger replica angles reduce norm sensitivity in the balanced case; more replicas improve generalization in the unbalanced case.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeting wide regions of the MSE landscape through constrained replicas can improve their center classifier's generalization on Gaussian mixtures.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: The study concerns a convex single-unit classifier on synthetic Gaussian mixtures, and the authors caution that the findings may not carry over as-is to deep networks. Some results are presented in plots without numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. Plot values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under comparable tuning. Different optimizers and epoch budgets across replica conditions do not isolate optimizer effects.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict follows for V7 from changing both the flatness construct and the outcome from generalization gap to test error. The supplied text supports the related findings, but they do not test a listed claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness, its comparison with norm- and margin-based measures, and the specified convolutional-family settings.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: threshold-linear classifier (single-unit neural network)
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized local-entropy curves for reference configurations from regularized MSE optimization with different regularization strengths.
rows.measure: Normalized local entropy as a function of distance; compared with generalization properties of the reference configurations.
rows.value: Reference configurations with better generalization properties have higher local entropy curves.
rows.note: The paper states the comparison; plot-specific curve values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The reported local-entropy association is supported, but cannot establish any listed version. Regularization changes training error as well as generalization; this is not V7's comparison among similarly fitted networks.

rows.subject: threshold-linear classifier (single-unit neural network)
rows.size_stated: N-dimensional weights; numerical results use N = 1000
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized local-entropy curves for reference configurations from regularized MSE optimization with different bias and norm choices.
rows.measure: Normalized local entropy as a function of squared distance; compared with generalization properties of the reference configurations.
rows.value: Reference configurations with better generalization properties have higher local entropy curves.
rows.note: The paper attributes better generalization to particular fine-tuned bias and λ values; plot-specific values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The association is supported but measures no listed version. Figure 3 selects each fixed bias's norm to minimize generalization error; that selection should be explicit. N = 1000 applies to numerical generalization results in the left panel, not the analytical local-entropy curves.

rows.subject: center of y = 10 threshold-linear classifier replicas
rows.operation_detail: Measured center generalization error while varying replica norm and angle.
rows.measure: Generalization error of the replica center as a function of replica norm.
rows.baseline: The θ = 0 limit reproduces results of a single device.
rows.value: With sufficiently large angles, generalization is nearly optimal and dependence on norm is mild; increasing θ reduces norm dependence.
rows.uncertainty: Numerical points averaged over 30 samples; error bars shown in figure.
rows.note: The authors qualify the result as applying to this simple model and state that the phenomenon may not carry over as-is to deep networks.
rows.check: This compares the study's replica method with a single classifier and belongs under fits_no_version. The reported near-optimal generalization is supported; the caution about transfer to deep networks does not justify a partial state.

rows.subject: center of y threshold-linear classifier replicas
rows.operation_detail: Measured center generalization error while increasing the number of replicas at fixed mutual angle.
rows.measure: Generalization error of the replica center.
rows.baseline: Typical minimizer of the norm-regularized MSE loss; y = 1 is the single-device case.
rows.value: Increasing the number of replicas improves generalization; the large-y limit is indistinguishable from y = 10.
rows.uncertainty: Numerical samples: 100, 30, and 20 for y = 1, 3, and 10 respectively.
rows.note: The text reports analytical curves and numerical results; figure-specific error values are not transcribed.
rows.check: This is performance of the study's replica method against its single-device baseline, rather than a result on a listed version. The improvement with more replicas is supported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
